subject.title: WhatsApp inbound messages not received in k3s nested container (outbound works)

question: Should WhatsApp external-inbound loss be solved with active liveness probing, provider-side reconnect backfill, explicit unrecoverable-gap diagnostics, or a combined policy?
rationale: Current source shows only bounded event-driven catch-up, while the remaining symptom spans transport liveness, provider history semantics, read receipts, privacy, and live WhatsApp proof that automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Combined recovery design
options.body: Design a plugin-owned policy with active post-reconnect liveness, bounded monitored-chat backfill where reliable, and explicit gap warnings when messages cannot be recovered.

options.title: Warn-only diagnostics first
options.body: Add status and log diagnostics for inbound-stream gaps without attempting history replay until WhatsApp/Baileys backfill behavior is proven live.

options.title: Keep append-only scope
options.body: Declare the bounded append catch-up behavior sufficient and close broader inbound-loss work only after maintainers explicitly accept that remaining container/zombie cases are outside scope.

recommendation.title: Combined recovery design
recommendation.body: Design a plugin-owned policy with active post-reconnect liveness, bounded monitored-chat backfill where reliable, and explicit gap warnings when messages cannot be recovered.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent durable inbound work and the maintainer comment on the remaining provider-side gap make this the best available routing candidate.
